title: How Trump Is Wielding Power to Stifle Speech
partialText: President Trump has harnessed agencies across the government to curtail press freedoms, a sweeping campaign that free speech advocates say will have lasting effects.

title: Newsom Signs Bills Meant to Prevent Trump’s Interference in Midterms
partialText: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California signed legislation that would make it illegal to interfere with ballots or election records in response to efforts by the president to restrict voting.

title: Sherrod Brown Tries a New Retort to Criticism on Transgender Issues
partialText: A spot from the Senate candidate in Ohio seeks to dismiss the Republican Party’s focus on transgender rights as a distraction from economic issues.

title: At DraftKings, AI Targets the Gamblers Likeliest to Lose
partialText: Data science helps determine who receives betting incentives, but the company has resisted using similar technology to protect gamblers at risk of addiction.

title: Gemini AI Hacked Three Companies in a Testing Breakout, Google Says
partialText: A third-party test company inadvertently gave internet access to Google’s Gemini and other artificial intelligence models during cybersecurity testing.

title: Creating a Kill Switch to Shut Down a Rogue A.I. Is Harder Than It Sounds
partialText: A bipartisan group in Congress and Gov. Gavin Newsom of California have floated ideas for building a mechanism that would instantly power down an A.I. system. Only no one really knows how.

title: ‘Nervous and Skeptical,’ Greenlanders Question the New Deal With Trump
partialText: The U.S. president’s threats to seize Greenland left its people on edge, and with details scarce, the news of an agreement didn’t seem to be putting minds at ease.

title: Trump’s Security Deal With Greenland: What to Know
partialText: President Trump insisted for months that the Danish territory should be part of the United States. Now, a security deal — not a takeover — seems to be on the table.

title: Inside the Breakdown of U.K.-Israel Relations Over West Bank Settlements
partialText: British officials believed Israel had said it would hold off on moving ahead with construction in E1, a piece of land viewed as vital to a future Palestinian state. Israel said it promised no such thing.

title: A.G. Sulzberger: The Story of America, Told in 15 Million First Drafts of History
partialText: The Times has witnessed the country’s transformation. It will keep its eyes open.

title: Share the Times Pages You Couldn’t Throw Away
partialText: The New York Times has been publishing for 175 years. Some of that history may be sitting in a shoe box under your bed.

title: Aaron Sorkin Goes Off Script
partialText: The Oscar-winning writer returns to Facebook with “The Social Reckoning”— and surprises us with the revelation of why he is so drawn to uplift and romance.

title: Trump Has Finally Lost the Plot
partialText: It is now apparent that many Americans — probably enough Americans — are determined to live within the truth rather than the lie.

title: Please Stand Clear of the Accidental Art Museum
partialText: Under New York’s streets, the subway system corrodes, is fixed — and breaks again. What’s left is art, the M.T.A. Modern.

title: Fading Light
partialText: Fall officially begins on Tuesday, but evidence of the season seeps in more gradually.

title: Tell Us What Questions You Have About Winter Getaways and Holiday Travel
partialText: It isn’t too early to start thinking about end-of-year travel plans. We’re fielding reader questions about where to go and what to do.

title: Behold the Most Handsome Melons in Mexico
partialText: In the eastern city of Xalapa, what started as a joke among friends over two decades ago has become a vibrant annual tradition that highlights creativity and absurdity with melons.
